text:
nina: quick note from the eval lab: Atria-13B quant experiments are showing a weird long-context recall drop at int4 and a smaller drift at int6. thinking about routing rules + shadow plan.

kevin: sketch the numbers pls.

nina: pasted mini-table from local run (3k conv sessions, mixed-turn longprompts):

```
Model         | mode  | p50  | p95  | cost / 1M toks | core_recall_delta
Atria-13B     | fp16  | 120ms| 260ms| $14.0          | baseline
Atria-13B     | int6  | 130ms| 280ms| $9.0           | -0.6%
Atria-13B     | int4  | 170ms| 520ms| $5.2           | -3.5% (long prompts >2048)
```

priya: long prompts? how many tokens pushing >2048 in sample?

nina: ~9% of sessions. those sessions are the majority of recall regressions. int4 causes spill to CPU and occasional recompile causing tail.

rachel: are these user-visible regressions or internal metrics?

nina: core_recall_delta is exact-match on our long-answer tests + safety unchanged. users would see omissions on multi-step Q&A occasionally.

kevin: what's the priming effect here? do we see token inflation?

nina: priming adds ~12% tokens/session for this UX (session-level priming). economic gap shrinks: int6 vs fp16 saves ~30% nominal, but after priming ~25%. int4 nominal saves ~63%, after priming ~55% but quality hit is large for the risky slice.

priya: recommendation then?

nina: proposal: primary=int6 for mixed/long interactive (good cost/quality balance), fallback=fp16 for low-confidence or >2048 seq, int4 only for bulk rerank and short-turn bursts. plus gating by a length+confidence rule.

kevin: how to implement gating?

nina: simple rules to start:
- if prompt_seq_len > 2048 -> force fp16
- else if model_confidence (token entropy proxy) < 0.80 -> route to fp16
- else if batch_rerank_job -> allow int4
- otherwise -> serve int6

rachel: should we consider a hybrid per-token fallback (keep KV cache on int6 and call fp16 for risky spans)? that's more complex.

priya: ops constraints? infra-bot, anything special for int4 nodes?

infra-bot: note: int4 instances require different memory alloc and larger host-pinned buffers. enable staggered autoscale and tune GC thresholds.

kevin: agree with staggered rollout. propose shadow test: 3% traffic, 7 days, primary=int6, shadow=fp16 for sessions routed to int6; collect top-k recall delta and support-signal. compute priming-adjusted unit cost.

nina: canary KPIs (stop/rollback if any fail):
- mean_core_recall_delta > 1.0%
- p95 latency > SLA (450ms)
- production error rate increase > 0.1%
- net cost savings < 15% after priming adj

priya: we should also capture per-segment signal (short vs long) and show the delta table to product so they can decide.

kevin: also log per-session token counts and which rule fired (length vs confidence). helps tune thresholds.

nina: action items:
- kevin: set up 3% 7-day shadow (tomorrow) and wire metrics into dashboard
- priya: prepare GTN blurb: "Atria-13B: recommended int6 for interactive; fp16 fallback for long/risky; int4 for batch rerank" + numbers
- rachel: run a focused 500-sample manual check on long prompts to characterize hallucination modes on int4

kevin: will do. infra-bot: schedule shadow job when ready.

infra-bot: shadow job queued: sj-2026-17.

nina: thanks team. planning to present summary to product tomorrow AM. :)
